 Dated this the 02nd day of December, 2016
 Judgment
Petitioner is a wholesale dealer in food-grains, doing business under the name and style 'Kottumala Traders'.
According to the petitioner, petitioner is having necessary license, under the Food Safety and Standards Act and attendant Rules and Regulations.
However on 31.10.2016, petitioner purchased wheat from another company, evident from Ext.P5 invoice.
On 03.11.2016, out of the wheat purchased as per Ext.P5, petitioner sold wheat to another company in Kollam, as per Ext.P8 invoices.

While the wheat being transported in lorry bearing registration No.KL-05-AB 1764, the same was intercepted by the Police, and took into custody the lorry as well as the product, alleging that the W.P.(C). NO. 36513 OF 2016 wheat transported are rationed articles.

A crime was registered as Crime No. 2918 by the Kottiyam Police, alleging offences under Sections 3 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, read with Clause 5(A) of the Kerala Rationing Order, evident from Ext.P9 FIR.

According to the petitioner, the wheat was purchased by the petitioner from outside agencies, which was sold by the Food Corporation of India to the dealer, and there is no manner of liability for the petitioner, as per the provisions of the Essential Commodities Act, and the Kerala Rationing Order.
Therefore, there shall be a direction to release the wheat to the petitioner.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Senior Government Pleader and perused the documents on record and the pleadings put forth by the respective parties.
3.
The subject matter relates to an enquiry contemplated under Section 6A of the Essential Commodities Act.
Since the enquiry is pending before the statutory authority, under the Essential Commodities Act, I W.P.(C).
NO. 36513 OF 2016 do not think, it is proper on the part of this Court to interfere at the intervening stage.

However, petitioner has a clear cut contention that the wheat transported and intercepted by the police, consequent to which the crime was registered is purchased by the petitioner from the open market, and therefore, ultimately on enquiry, if it is found that it has no bearing with the provisions of the Essential Commodities Act, or the Kerala Rationing Order, petitioner is entitled as of right to get the invoice value of the product.
